interest: This file offers a compelling view of how routine scientific and administrative collaboration in agricultural biosecurity persisted between the United States and Japan in 1938 despite mounting geopolitical tensions surrounding the Second Sino-Japanese War. It notably documents the active enforcement of the Stimson Doctrine of non-recognition within the U.S. government, revealing how the State Department monitored other federal agencies—such as the Department of Agriculture—to prevent bureaucratic acquiescence to Japan's puppet state of 'Manchukuo'. Furthermore, the comprehensive digest of Japanese plant quarantine regulations (B.E.P.Q.-470) provides valuable historical insights into interwar phytosanitary regimes, quarantine law, and the global mapping of insect pests and plant blights across the Pacific basin.
keywords: Bureau of Entomology and Plant Quarantine
overview: This file (894.612/17 – 894.612/19) encompasses diplomatic correspondence, interdepartmental memoranda, and official regulatory digests from March to December 1938 concerning Japanese plant-quarantine import restrictions and reciprocal exchanges of quarantine legislation between the United States and Japan. The file begins with a State Department memorandum regarding the Department of Agriculture's use of the unrecognized name 'Manchukuo' instead of 'Manchuria' in an informational circular, followed by instructions distributing circular B.E.P.Q.-470 to the American Embassy and consulates in Japan. The circular itself sets forth Japanese Plant Quarantine Law No. 11 of 1914, Department Ordinance No. 27, inspection rules, and strict import bans on host plants and fruits to prevent the introduction of harmful pests such as the Mediterranean fruit fly, melon fly, and codling moth. The latter part of the file documents a November 1938 initiative by the Japanese Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, via the Japanese Embassy in Washington, presenting Japan's plant quarantine laws and requesting American regulations in return, which the State Department and USDA fulfilled in December 1938.

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum concerning the Department of Agriculture's use of the term 'Manchukuo' in a plant quarantine circular in violation of U.S. non-recognition policy.
keywords: Bureau of Entomology and Plant Quarantine
subfiles.summary: Mr. Myers of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs reports calling Mr. Hoyt, Assistant Chief of the Bureau of Entomology and Plant Quarantine, regarding the circular 'Plant-Quarantine Import Restrictions of Japan'. Myers pointed out that the circular used the term 'Manchukuo', whereas the State Department uses 'Manchuria' in accordance with the United States policy of non-recognition. Hoyt concurred with the guidance for future publications and agreed to inform Department of Agriculture officials, while Myers requested that the matter remain confidential without publicity.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Myers regarding use of the term 'Manchukuo' in Department of Agriculture publication
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs files

subfiles.about: Instruction No. 1451 from the Secretary of State transmitting the USDA plant-quarantine digest of Japan to the American Ambassador in Tokyo.
keywords: Bureau of Entomology and Plant Quarantine
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits to the American Ambassador in Tokyo a copy of digest B.E.P.Q.-470 on the plant-quarantine import restrictions of Japan. The instruction notes that an additional copy has been sent to the Consulate General at Tokyo, alongside extra copies intended for transmission to other American consular posts throughout Japan.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1451 to the American Ambassador at Tokyo transmitting plant-quarantine digest

subfiles.about: Instruction from the Secretary of State transmitting copies of the USDA plant-quarantine digest to the American Consular Officer in charge at Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits to the American Consular Officer in charge at Tokyo a copy of B.E.P.Q.-470 outlining Japan's plant-quarantine import restrictions. Additional copies are enclosed with instructions to forward them to other American consular offices in Japan for their information.
subfiles.title: Instruction to the American Consular Officer in Charge at Tokyo transmitting plant-quarantine digest
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in charge, Tokyo

subfiles.about: United States Department of Agriculture circular B.E.P.Q.-470 digesting the plant-quarantine import restrictions and legislation of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Prepared by Harry B. Shaw and reviewed by the Director of the Imperial Plant Quarantine Service in Yokohama, this circular details Japanese Plant Quarantine Law No. 11 of 1914 and Department Ordinance No. 27 as amended. It enumerates categories of plants requiring customs inspection, specifies worldwide geographical prohibitions on fruits, vegetables, and tubers to exclude injurious pests like the Mediterranean fruit fly and melon fly, and explains the conditions for mail entry, certificate exemptions, and import waivers.
subfiles.title: Circular B.E.P.Q.-470: Plant-Quarantine Import Restrictions of Japan
subfiles.to: Inspectors in Charge, nurserymen, and exporters

subfiles.about: Diplomatic note No. 203 from the Japanese Ambassador presenting Japanese plant quarantine regulations and requesting copies of corresponding United States regulations.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador informs the Secretary of State that the Bureau of Agriculture of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry wishes to present a copy of Japan's 'Law and Regulations concerning Plant Quarantine Service' to the USDA Bureau of Entomology and Plant Quarantine. The note requests that the enclosure be delivered to the Bureau and asks whether the United States Government can reciprocally furnish copies of its own plant quarantine laws and regulations.
subfiles.title: Note No. 203 from the Japanese Ambassador proposing exchange of plant quarantine laws

subfiles.about: Letter from the Secretary of State transmitting the Japanese Embassy's note and plant quarantine regulations to the Secretary of Agriculture.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State forwards to the Secretary of Agriculture a copy of note No. 203 from the Japanese Ambassador dated November 14, 1938, along with the enclosed Japanese plant quarantine regulations. The Secretary of State asks whether the Department of Agriculture can supply copies of United States laws and regulations on the subject to satisfy the Japanese Government's request.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of Agriculture regarding Japanese quarantine regulations

subfiles.about: Letter from the Acting Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of State enclosing United States plant quarantine statutes and orders for transmission to Japan.
keywords: Bureau of Entomology and Plant Quarantine
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of Agriculture acknowledges the State Department's letter of November 18 and conveys the thanks of the Chief of the Bureau of Entomology and Plant Quarantine for the Japanese regulations. Enclosed for transmission to the Japanese Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry are copies of the Plant Quarantine Act of August 20, 1912, as amended, lists of current quarantines, export certification regulations, and foreign quarantine texts.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Acting Secretary of Agriculture transmitting U.S. plant quarantine laws

subfiles.about: Diplomatic note from the Acting Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador transmitting United States plant quarantine publications.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of State replies to the Japanese Ambassador's note No. 203 of November 14, 1938, conveying the appreciation of the Chief of the Bureau of Entomology and Plant Quarantine for the Japanese quarantine laws. In return, the note transmits copies of the Plant Quarantine Act of 1912 as amended, current quarantine lists, sanitary export certification rules, and foreign plant quarantine orders for delivery to the Japanese Bureau of Agriculture.
subfiles.title: Note from the Acting Secretary of State to the Japanese Ambassador transmitting U.S. quarantine publications
